# Explanation of report workflow

This runfile is where we can run all the code required for the analysis, which will populate our environment with objects used in the format file. We typically run as much of the more heavier computation in the runfile as possible so that it doesn't take long to render the format file, since we may need to render iteratively as we adjust the format, fix typos, write explanatory notes, or add report sections.

`03-bulkRNA_GS.runfile.Rmd` computes gene set analyses, including GSEA and GSVA. In the future, this may include other interesting plots and/or analyses such as pathway/network analyses once they are automatable

## Custom functions....
```{r}
## I know, I am trying to get rid of functions. But this is a super useful one for automation.
### Store code as functions when the input is something you want to share in the format file
getSourceText <- function(func,a,b) {
  src <- attr(func, "srcref") # pull out function text
  if (is.null(src)) {return("Something went wrong. Ensure R session has `options(keep.source = TRUE)`")}
  raw_text <- as.character(src)
  trim_text <- tail(head(raw_text, -a), -b) # remove lines that encode extra function info 
  formatted_text <- paste(trim_text, collapse = "\n") # convert function text to string
  return(formatted_text)
}

# My group names in the strip text are too long, so I am labeling them with
# a newline
newLineLabel <- function(string) {
  string <- gsub("\\."," \n",string)
  string
}
```

## 0.3 - Prep gene set lists
```{r}
geneSets <- list()

geneSets[["H"]] <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "H") %>%
  dplyr::select(gene_symbol, gs_name) %>% unstack()

geneSets[["GOBP"]] <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", subcollection = "C5", subcategory = "GO:BP") %>%
  dplyr::select(gene_symbol, gs_name) %>% unstack()

geneSets[["CP"]] <- c(
  msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", subcollection = "C2", subcategory = "CP:BIOCARTA") %>%
    dplyr::select(gene_symbol, gs_name) %>% unstack(),
  msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", subcollection = "C2", subcategory = "CP:KEGG_LEGACY") %>%
    dplyr::select(gene_symbol, gs_name) %>% unstack(),
  msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", subcollection = "C2", subcategory = "CP:PID") %>%
    dplyr::select(gene_symbol, gs_name) %>% unstack(),
  msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", subcollection = "C2", subcategory = "CP:REACTOME") %>%
    dplyr::select(gene_symbol, gs_name) %>% unstack(),
  msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", subcollection = "C2", subcategory = "CP:WIKIPATHWAYS") %>%
    dplyr::select(gene_symbol, gs_name) %>% unstack()
)

# deduplicate genes
geneSets <- lapply(geneSets, FUN = function(x){
  lapply(x, function(x){
    gs <- x[!duplicated(x)]
  })
})

```

# 1 - GSEA

## 1.1 - Pre-rank DE stats

```{r}
bulk$gsea$stats <- bulk$gsea$resTab %>%
  filter(!is.na(pvalue)) %>%
  mutate(rank_stat = log2FoldChange * -log10(pvalue + .Machine$double.xmin)) %>% 
  split(.$contrast) %>%
    lapply(., function(y) {
      y %>% select(gene, rank_stat) %>%
        deframe() %>%
        sort()
    })
```

## 1.2 - Run GSEA
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
for(i in c("H","GOBP","CP")){
  res <- bulk$gsea$stats %>%
    lapply(., function(stats_vec) {
      fgsea(pathways = geneSets[[i]], stats = stats_vec,
            minSize = 15) %>% 
        arrange(pval)
  })
  bulk$gsea$results[[i]] <- lapply(res, function(contrast) {
    contrast %>%
      as_tibble() %>%
      rowwise() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(leading_edge = paste(leadingEdge, collapse = ", ")) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(n_leading_edge = str_count(leading_edge, pattern = ",") + 1,
                 #   leadingEdge = NULL,
                    database = i)
    })
}
```

## 1.2 - subset significant pathways
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=10}
# get top 30 pathways per contrast per database
for(i in c("H","GOBP","CP")){
  bulk$gsea$sigResults[[i]] <- lapply(bulk$gsea$results[[i]], function(x){
    df <- x %>%
      as_tibble() %>%
      filter(pval < 0.1) %>%
      flag_redundant_leading_edge(threshold = 1) %>% # this line flags redundant pathways
      dplyr::mutate(term = str_replace_all(string = pathway, 
                                           pattern = "_", 
                                           replacement = " "),
                    propLEG = n_leading_edge/size) %>%
      arrange(rev(propLEG),padj) %>%
      slice_max(propLEG,n = 30, with_ties = FALSE) 
  })
}

```

## 1.3 - make plots
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=10}
# make plots
for(j in c("H","GOBP","CP")){
  for(i in unique(bulk$gsea$resTab$contrast)){
    bulk$plots$gsea[[j]][[i]] <- bulk$gsea$sigResults[[j]][[i]] %>%
      filter(!redundant_leading_edge) %>%          # filter out redundant pathways
      ggplot(aes(x = NES, y = fct_reorder(term, NES), 
                 size = propLEG,          # proportion of leading-edge genes per set
                 #size = n_leading_edge,  # absolute number of leading-edge genes
                 color = pval)) +
      geom_point() + ggtitle(paste(i,j,sep = "_")) +
      scale_color_gradient(low = "red", high = "blue") +
      theme_bw(base_size = 8) +
      #scale_size_continuous(limits = c(0,1), name = "leading edge\n--------\ntotal genes") +
      scale_y_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(40), limits = rev) +
      ylab(NULL) +  
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
            aspect.ratio = 1) +
      xlim(min(bind_rows(bulk$gsea$sigResults[[j]])$NES),
           max(bind_rows(bulk$gsea$sigResults[[j]])$NES)) +
      force_panelsizes(cols = unit(8, "cm"))
  }}

```

## 1.2&3 - pull out sig pathways and make plots at once
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=10}
bulk$plots$gsea <- lapply(bulk$gsea$results, function(x){
df <- bind_rows(lapply(x, function(y){
    df <- y %>%
      as_tibble() %>%
      filter(pval < 0.1) %>%
      flag_redundant_leading_edge(threshold = 1) %>%  # this line flags redundant pathways
      dplyr::mutate(term = str_replace_all(string = pathway, 
                                           pattern = "_", 
                                           replacement = " "),
                    propLEG = n_leading_edge/size) %>%
      arrange(rev(propLEG),padj) %>%
      slice_max(propLEG,n = 30, with_ties = FALSE) 
  }), .id = "contrast")
plots <- list()
  for(i in unique(bulk$gsea$resTab$contrast)){
 plots[[i]] <- df %>%
    filter(contrast %in% i) %>%
    filter(!redundant_leading_edge) %>% # this line removes redundant pathways
    ggplot(aes(x = NES, y = fct_reorder(term, NES), 
                 size = propLEG,          # proportion of leading-edge genes per set
                 #size = n_leading_edge,  # absolute number of leading-edge genes
                 color = pval)) +
      geom_point() + ggtitle(paste(i,j,sep = "_")) +
      scale_color_gradient(low = "red", high = "blue") +
      theme_bw(base_size = 8) +
      #scale_size_continuous(limits = c(0,1), name = "leading edge\n--------\ntotal genes") +
      scale_y_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(40), limits = rev) +
      ylab(NULL) +  
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
            aspect.ratio = 1) +
      xlim(min(df$NES),
           max(df$NES)) +
      force_panelsizes(cols = unit(8, "cm"))
}
return(plots)
})

```

## 1.4 - Compare Leading Edge Gene Expression
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
### Initialize Plots storage
bulk[["plots"]][['gsea_leadingEdgeHM']] = list()

### Get Gene table
gene_tbl <- bulk$degTab$limma

### for each database (db), and for each comparison (i), and for each top/bottom 3 pathways (j), create heatmap of leading edge genes
for(db in names(bulk[["gsea"]][["results"]])){  

  ### initialize database specific heatmaps
  bulk[["plots"]][['gsea_leadingEdgeHM']][[db]] = list()
  
  for(i in colnames(bulk$md$contr.matrix)){
  
    ### initialize contrast specific results
    bulk[["plots"]][['gsea_leadingEdgeHM']][[db]][[i]] = list()
    
    ### Get Contrast Matrix
    cmSubset <- bulk$md$contr.matrix %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      rownames_to_column("group") %>%
      dplyr::select(group, "comparison" = all_of(i))
    
    
    for(j in bulk[["gsea"]][["sigResults"]][[db]][[i]] %>%
        filter(!redundant_leading_edge) %>% # this line removes redundant pathways
    arrange(desc(NES)) %>%
    {
        bind_rows(
            filter(., NES > 0) %>% slice_head(n = 3),
            filter(., NES < 0) %>% slice_tail(n = 3)
        )
    } %>% .$pathway){
      
      ### Get leading edge genes
      genes = bulk[["gsea"]][["sigResults"]][[db]][[i]][which(bulk[["gsea"]][["sigResults"]][[db]][[i]]$pathway == j),]$leadingEdge  %>% unlist()
      
      bulk[["plots"]][['gsea_leadingEdgeHM']][[db]][[i]][[j]] = plotHeatmap(bulk = bulk,
                   genes = genes,
                   method = 'limma',
                   contrast = i,
                   pairing_bar = TRUE,
                   comparison_borders = TRUE,
                   fdr = 0.05,
                   gene_order = 'none')


      
    }
  }
}
```

## 1.5 Leading Edge gene trajectories
```{r, fig.width=14, fig.height=16, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Long dataframe from CPM and sample data tables
dfCPM <- as.data.frame(bulk$dge$cpm) %>% 
  tibble::rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!gene, names_to = "sampleID", values_to = "cpmExpr") %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(.,bulk$dge$samples, by="sampleID") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(type = "sample") %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, sampleID, subjectID, grp, tPt, cpmExpr, type)

# Add averaged values per group and timepoint
dfCPM <- rbind(dfCPM, dfCPM %>%
                 dplyr::group_by(gene, grp, tPt) %>%
                 dplyr::summarize(cpmExpr = mean(cpmExpr)) %>%
                 dplyr::mutate(subjectID = paste(grp,"avg",sep = "."),
                               sampleID = paste(grp,"avg",tPt,sep = "."),
                               type = "avg"))


## I wanted manageable gaps between days for longitudinal plotting, so scaled manually
day_key <- as.data.frame(cbind(
  visit = unique(dfCPM$tPt),
  visitInt = as.numeric(gsub("V","",unique(dfCPM$tPt))), 
  visitIntAnnot = c("Visit1", "Visit2"), 
  modVisitInt = c(1,2))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(VisitInt = as.numeric(visitInt), 
                modVisitInt = as.numeric(modVisitInt))


# named vector for per-subject color code
subjectCol <- dfCPM %>% 
  dplyr::select(subjectID,grp) %>% 
  unique() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(color = case_when(
    grp == "H" ~ "tomato3",
    grp == "L" ~ "dodgerblue3")) %>% 
  dplyr::pull(color) %>% 
  setNames(unique(dfCPM$subjectID))

# named vector for group colors
groupCol <- c("H" = "tomato3",
              "L" = "dodgerblue3")

### Initialize Plots storage
bulk[["plots"]][['gsea_leadingEdgeTraj']] = list()

### for each database (db), and for each comparison (i), and for each top/bottom 3 pathways (j), create heatmap of leading edge genes
for(db in names(bulk[["gsea"]][["results"]])){  

  ### initialize database specific heatmaps
  bulk[["plots"]][['gsea_leadingEdgeTraj']][[db]] = list()
  
  for(i in colnames(bulk$md$contr.matrix)){
  
    ### initialize contrast specific results
    bulk[["plots"]][['gsea_leadingEdgeTraj']][[db]][[i]] = list()
    
    ### Get Contrast Matrix
    cmSubset <- bulk$md$contr.matrix %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      rownames_to_column("group") %>%
      dplyr::select(group, "comparison" = all_of(i))
    
    
    for(j in bulk[["gsea"]][["sigResults"]][[db]][[i]] %>%
        #flag_redundant_leading_edge(threshold = 1) %>% filter(!redundant_leading_edge) %>% # this line removes redundant pathways
        filter(!redundant_leading_edge) %>% # this line removes redundant pathways
    arrange(desc(NES)) %>%
    {
        bind_rows(
            filter(., NES > 0) %>% slice_head(n = 3),
            filter(., NES < 0) %>% slice_tail(n = 3)
        )
    } %>% .$pathway){
      
      ### Get 20 leading edge genes
      geneVec = bulk[["gsea"]][["sigResults"]][[db]][[i]][which(bulk[["gsea"]][["sigResults"]][[db]][[i]]$pathway == j),]$leadingEdge  %>% unlist() %>% .[1:20]
      
      ### Plot trajectories
      bulk[["plots"]][['gsea_leadingEdgeTraj']][[db]][[i]][[j]] = dfCPM %>%
  dplyr::filter(gene %in% geneVec) %>% 
  full_join(as.data.frame(day_key), by = c("tPt" = "visit")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    gene = factor(gene, levels = geneVec)
  ) %>%
  {
    ggplot(
      .,
      aes(
        x = modVisitInt,
        y = cpmExpr,
        color = subjectID,
        fill = grp
      )
    ) +
      theme_classic() +
      theme(
        legend.position = "top",
        axis.text.x = element_text(
          angle = 90,
          vjust = 0.5,
          hjust = 1
        )
      ) +
      
      # Injection days
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = c(1, 2),
        size = .3,
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = "black"
      ) +
      
      geom_line(
        aes(
          linewidth = type,
          alpha = type
        )
      ) +
      
      scale_linewidth_manual(
        values = c(
          "avg" = 0.8,
          "sample" = 0.1
        )
      ) +
      
      scale_alpha_manual(
        values = c(
          "avg" = 1,
          "sample" = 0.5
        )
      ) +
      
      # Point only at the final visit for each subject
      geom_point(
        data = ~ .x %>%
          dplyr::group_by(subjectID, gene) %>%
          dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() == 1) %>%
          dplyr::ungroup(),
        aes(
          fill = grp,
          alpha = type
        ),
        shape = 21,
        size = 2
      ) +
      
      scale_color_manual(
        values = subjectCol,
        drop = FALSE
      ) +
      
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = groupCol,
        drop = FALSE,
        guide = guide_legend(
          override.aes = list(
            alpha = 1,
            shape = 21,
            color = NA,
            size = 3
          )
        )
      ) +
      
      labs(
        title = paste(i, " DEGs"),
        x = "Visits",
        y = "CPM",
        fill = "Group"
      ) +
      
      guides(
        color = "none",
        alpha = "none",
        linewidth = "none"
      ) +
      
      scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = unique(day_key$modVisitInt),
        labels = unique(day_key$visitIntAnnot)
      ) +
      
      facet_wrap(
        ~gene,
        ncol = 4,
        scales = "free_y"
      )
  }
      
    }
  }
}
```

# 2 - GSVA

## 2.1 - Run GSVA 
```{r}
for(i in c("H","GOBP","CP")){
bulk$gsva$param[[i]] <- gsvaParam(bulk$gsva$exprTab, geneSets[[i]], minSize = 15)
bulk$gsva$results[[i]] <- gsva(bulk$gsva$param[[i]])
}
```

## 2.2 - Make GSVA heatmaps of variable gene sets
```{r}
bulk$plots$gsva$varPaths <- list()

for(i in c("H","GOBP","CP")){
# pull out variable pathways and order
  df <- as.data.frame(bulk$gsva$results[[i]]) %>%
    mutate(var=rowVars(as.matrix(select(., everything())), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    arrange(desc(var)) %>%
    slice_head(n=30) %>% select(!var)
  ord <- hclust(dist(df))$order
  
# long dataframe for ggplot2
  bulk$plots$gsva$varPaths[[i]] <- df %>%
    rownames_to_column("pathway") %>%
    pivot_longer(!pathway,
                 names_to = "sampleID",
                 values_to = "Enrichment") %>%
    inner_join(.,bulk$dge$samples[,c('sampleID',"subjectID","group")],
               by="sampleID") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(pathway) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(zscore = scale(Enrichment)[,1]) %>% 
    ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::arrange(group,subjectID) %>%    # so samples are organized by these variables
    dplyr::mutate(
      group = factor(group, levels = unique(group)),
      subjectID = factor(subjectID, levels = unique(subjectID)),
      pathway = factor(pathway, levels = unique(pathway)[ord]),
      term = str_replace_all(string = pathway, 
                             pattern = "_", 
                             replacement = " "),
      term = str_split_fixed(term, " ", n=2)[,2],
      term = factor(term, levels = unique(term)[ord]),
      group = gsub(".", " ",group, fixed = TRUE)
      ) %>%
    ggplot(., aes(x = subjectID, 
                 # fill = Enrichment, 
                  fill = zscore,
                  y = term)) +
    geom_tile(show.legend = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low="dodgerblue3", mid="white", high="tomato") +
    facet_grid(~ group, 
               scales='free_x', space="fixed",
               labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 4)) +
    labs(title = paste0(i," Pathway Enrichment"),
         x = "Sample", 
         y = "Pathway") +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(50), limits = rev) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 8) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1,color = "black"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
          legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

## 2.3 - Make GSVA heatmaps based on GSEA pathways
```{r}
# pull out GSEA pathways that were visualized in dot plots per contrast

for(j in colnames(bulk$md$contr.matrix)){
  cmSubset <-bulk$md$contr.matrix %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("group") %>%
    dplyr::select("group","comparison" = all_of(j))
 
  for(i in c("H","GOBP","CP")){
    df <- as.data.frame(bulk$gsva$results[[i]]) %>%
      rownames_to_column("pathway") %>%
      filter(pathway %in% bulk$gsea$sigResults[[i]][[j]]$pathway)
      
     
    ord <- hclust(dist(select(df,!pathway)))$order
      
    bulk$plots$gsva$contrasts[[i]][[j]] <- df %>%
      pivot_longer(!pathway,
                   names_to = "sampleID",
                   values_to = "Enrichment") %>%
    inner_join(.,bulk$dge$samples[,c('sampleID',"subjectID","group")],
               by="sampleID") %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(.,cmSubset, by = "group") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(pathway) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(zscore = scale(Enrichment)[,1]) %>% 
    ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::arrange(group,subjectID) %>%    # so samples are organized by these variables
    dplyr::mutate(
      group = factor(group, levels = unique(group)),
      subjectID = factor(subjectID, levels = unique(subjectID)),
      pathway = factor(pathway, levels = unique(pathway)[ord]),
      term = str_replace_all(string = pathway, 
                             pattern = "_", 
                             replacement = " "),
      term = str_split_fixed(term, " ", n=2)[,2],
      term = factor(term, levels = unique(term)[ord]),
      group = gsub(".", " ",group, fixed = TRUE)) %>%
      {
      ggplot(., aes(x = subjectID, y = term, fill = Enrichment)) +
      geom_tile(show.legend = TRUE) +
      scale_fill_gradient2(low="dodgerblue3", mid="white", high="tomato") +
      facet_grid(~ group, 
                 scales='free_x', space="fixed",
                 labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 4)) +
      labs(title = paste0(i," Pathway Enrichment"),
           subtitle = paste0("Contrast: ", j),
           x = "Sample", 
           y = "Pathway") +
      scale_y_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(50), limits = rev) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 8) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)) +
      geom_rect(data = subset(., comparison %in% c(1,-1)), 
                linewidth = 2, fill = NA, colour = "black", 
                xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf) 
      }
      
}}
```

### 2.3.1 - view hallmark GS by contrasts
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
bulk$plots$gsva$contrasts$H
```


# 3 - Export objects

## 3.1 - Prep for export
```{r prep for export}
## increase report count by 1
bulk$config$reportNumber <- sprintf("%02d", as.numeric(bulk$config$reportNumber) + 1)  

## make subdirectories for `outputs` and `rds`
subdir <- paste0("report-", bulk$config$reportNumber)

if (!dir.exists(here("outputs/", subdir))) {
  dir.create(here("outputs/", subdir))}

if (!dir.exists(here("rds/", subdir))) {
  dir.create(here("rds/", subdir))}
```

## 3.2 - Write `bulk` rds
```{r}
bulk %>%
  write_rds(., here("rds", subdir, paste0("bulk-", getDate(), ".rds")))
```

## 3.3 - Export GSEA results
```{r export, warning=FALSE}
resTab_filename_GSEA <- paste0(
  bulk$config$project, "-",
  bulk$config$reportNumber, "-",
  "GSEA_results-", getDate(), ".xlsx")

writexl::write_xlsx(lapply(bulk$gsea$results, function(x){bind_rows(x, .id = "contrast")}), here("outputs", subdir, resTab_filename_GSEA))
```

## 3.4 - Export GSVA results
```{r}

write.xlsx(list(
  "Hallmark" = rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(bulk$gsva$msigH.gsva),"pathway"),
  "Canonical" = rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(bulk$gsva$msigCP.gsva),"pathway"),
  "BiologicalProcess" = rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(bulk$gsva$msigGOBP.gsva),"pathway")),
  here("outputs", subdir, "GSVAresults.xlsx"))
```
